exercise.name: Lever Lying T-bar Row

reference.title: Lever Lying T-bar Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Chest-supported T-bar row machine (incline chest pad, plate-loaded lever with handles)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: row to the pad without lifting the chest.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Lie face down on the incline pad with the chest supported and the feet on the platform; take the lever handles, arms hanging straight.
Breathe out and row the handles up toward the lower ribs, elbows travelling back close to the body.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together with the chest still on the pad.
Breathe in and lower the lever along its arc until the arms are straight.
Let the shoulder blades spread at the bottom without losing the pad.

mistakes.fix: Keep the chest on the pad; lighten the plates.
Drive the elbows back, shoulders down.
Lower to straight arms each rep.
Keep the chin just over the pad, neck long.

kinematics.peak: ≈133° at the top of the row
kinematics.norm: From straight arms to well bent at the lower ribs (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Elbows 24.4 cm from the shoulders, beside the trunk
kinematics.norm: Elbows travel from in front of the shoulders to beside the trunk (clinical opinion)
Neutral or pronated on the lever handles, about shoulder width (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 105.2 cm high, 94.4 cm ahead of the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 22.5°; hands within 0.62 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handles ride an arc about a pivot near the floor at the far end of the machine (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Chest on the 40° pad, feet planted
kinematics.norm: Chest supported: little spinal load compared with bent-over rowing (Fenwick 2009)

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms hanging
kinematics.peak: 1.3 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down
kinematics.norm: About 1.2 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #3783, Lever Lying T-bar Row, video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Plate load is user-chosen: start light and keep the chest on the pad.
Lower the lever onto its stop before stepping off.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Neck discomfort: rest the chin just over the top of the pad, look down.
progressions: Pause rows with a 2 s squeeze.

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together (Lehman 2004 for row muscle activity).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together (Lehman 2004 for row muscle activity).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk on the pad; chest support keeps their load low (Fenwick 2009).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk on the pad; chest support keeps their load low (Fenwick 2009).
